style: Product-quality render for a mobile app thumbnail. 3/4 front view, about 20 degrees elevation, subject fills roughly 70% of the shorter side, centred with breathing room. One soft key light upper-left, a rim light from back-right, gentle floor contact shadow. No lens flare, no glow, no bokeh props, no text, no UI, no device frame, no watermark. Faithful to the attached reference: keep the real model shapes and materials; clean up, relight and recompose only.

lighting.prompt: The battle-damaged sci-fi helmet of the attached reference — this exact model, and no other: a large curved visor of dark teal-green glass carrying faint cyan HUD glyphs, a glowing cyan ring lens and a small orange triangle marker, scuffed off-white armour plates with gold-brass trim along the jaw, and a segmented ear module with ribbed cables tucked behind. Three-quarter front-left view with the visor turned towards the camera, the helmet centred and filling about 70 percent of the frame height, cables kept behind the silhouette. Three coloured point lights are unmistakable: a warm orange lamp low on the left throwing a clear orange pool across the floor and tinting the left armour plates orange, a cool blue lamp low on the right throwing a blue pool and tinting the right plates blue, and a white key directly above putting a bright highlight on the crown. The two coloured pools overlap in front of the helmet. The visor still reads as teal-green glass under them. Demonstrates runtime light types.

No caption under the inset, no text anywhere. Demonstrates a second camera view rendered into the same frame

custom-geometry.prompt: The trefoil ribbon knot of the attached reference — exactly this shape, a (2,3) torus knot swept by a flat band that twists two and a half turns around the loop and whose width ripples six times along it, so the band passes in front of and behind itself three times. Polished SceneView-blue #005BC1 metal, glossy and slightly reflective, a bright specular highlight travelling along the band where it turns. Floating alone with a soft contact shadow, tilted so the lobes separate instead of reading as a flat rosette. Demonstrates a mesh whose vertices are generated in Kotlin at runtime.

lines-paths.prompt: The closed route of the attached reference — exactly this shape: a loop through eight control points arranged on a circle and lifted by two full sine periods, so it waves up and down twice round the ring. The route is a smooth swept tube of pale blue #A4C1FF with a real thickness and real shading, not a hairline. Eight purple #6446CD beads sit on the control points, a larger soft-lilac #D2A8FF sphere marker rides the route with a slightly fatter lilac trail behind it, and directly below, flat on the ground plane, the same eight points are drawn as a dashed straight-segment polyline in deep blue #005BC1. Seen from about 27 degrees above. No grid, no props. Demonstrates lines, paths, splines and point sets drawn as swept tube geometry.

ar-placement.prompt: An augmented-reality photo taken with a phone held at chest height: the green vintage toy car of the attached reference, standing on its draped rust-red satin cloth pedestal (the cloth and the car are one model, keep both exactly as in the reference: the chrome bumpers, the yellow flame decals, the tail fins), placed at its true small size, about 30 cm tall, on the wooden floor of a real lived-in living room, a sofa and a rug softly out of focus behind it. The object sits in the lower-middle of the frame, seen from about 30 degrees above, grounded by a soft contact shadow under the cloth. No placement ring, no reticle, no plane grid, no dots, no UI of any kind. Demonstrates a 3D model placed automatically on a real floor at real-world scale.

animation-physics.prompt: The low-poly fox of the attached reference — this exact model, and no other: a faceted orange-red body built from flat triangles, a paler cream muzzle and chest, dark chocolate-brown lower legs and paws, upright pointed ears and a thick orange tail with a cream tip. It is caught mid-stride in its walk cycle, one front paw lifted and the opposite hind leg reaching back, head up and slightly turned towards the camera, the tail streaming behind. Three-quarter side view from the front-left at about 15 degrees elevation, the fox centred and filling about 70 percent of the frame width, a soft contact shadow under each planted paw on a plain floor. The facets must stay flat and crisp: no fur, no photo-real texture, no extra detail. Demonstrates skeletal animation clips blended at runtime

billboard.prompt: The three shapes of the attached reference — exactly these, in this order from left to right: a rounded glossy blue cube, a mirror-polished gold metallic sphere reflecting a soft studio, and a matte coral-red cone. Above each hangs its own floating name label in the same colour, set in a clean rounded sans-serif: 'Player 1' in blue above the cube, 'Treasure' in golden yellow above the sphere, 'Enemy' in red above the cone. The camera is orbited about 35 degrees to the right and raised a little, so the three shapes are seen at an angle and recede in depth, while every label still faces the camera flat and square — the point of a billboard. The three labels are the only text in the image and are spelled exactly as given; keep them large and legible. The row fills about 80 percent of the frame width. Demonstrates labels that always turn to face the camera

occlusion-material.prompt: The glossy sky-blue metallic sphere of the attached reference — exactly this material: a smooth cyan-blue metal, strong soft studio highlights, a blurred reflection of a bright softbox. Only the upper two thirds of the sphere exist in the image: its lower third is cut away by an invisible upright panel standing just in front of it, so the sphere stops abruptly at a perfectly straight, crisp horizontal edge, like a dome, and below that edge there is only the plain empty background — no lower half, no seam, no reflection of the missing part, exactly as in the reference. Nothing is drawn where the panel is: no glass, no outline, no floor under the sphere, no shadow below the cut. Seen straight on at about 10 degrees elevation, the visible dome centred and filling about 65 percent of the frame height. Demonstrates an occlusion material, invisible geometry that hides what is behind it

video.prompt: The small video stage of the attached reference — exactly this layout: a wide 16:9 flat screen floating in front of a plain back wall, above a plain floor, playing a smooth diagonal gradient that runs from violet #6A40C8 to royal blue #0A5CC8 with soft angular light bands, which is the frame of the clip the demo plays. The screen is the only light source that matters: it glows evenly, throws a soft violet-blue spill onto the wall around it and a blurred violet-blue reflection onto the floor in front. Seen from slightly above and about 20 degrees to the left, the screen centred and filling about 75 percent of the frame width. No bezel, no stand, no play button, no progress bar, no people, no picture on the screen other than that gradient. Demonstrates a video playing as a texture on a 3D plane

double-pendulum.prompt: The double pendulum of the attached reference — exactly this rig, and no other: a slim graphite-grey vertical post standing on a square graphite base, a small chrome pivot ball at the top of the post, a straight lead arm in deep blue #005BC1 hanging from the pivot to a glossy blue ball joint, and from that joint a second straight arm in lighter blue #3D7BD6 ending in a larger glossy violet bob. There are exactly three balls in the image: the small chrome pivot, the blue joint and the violet bob — never a second bob. Caught mid-swing, the two arms folded at a sharp angle, and behind the violet bob a thin bright violet trail traces its chaotic looping path through the air in two or three tangled curves. It stands on a floor ruled with a faint square grid that fades into the distance. Three-quarter front view at about 15 degrees elevation, the rig slightly left of centre so the trail has room, the whole rig filling about 80 percent of the frame height. Demonstrates a chaotic double-pendulum simulation

contact-shadow-preview.prompt: Edit the attached real capture of the demo rather than inventing a new scene: keep its exact objects, positions, proportions and camera angle — two identical matte terracotta-orange cubes #B4693C and a flat black TV screen hung on the back wall. The left cube stands on the floor and keeps the soft grey contact shadow that darkens where it meets the floor and fades out within a short distance, a shadow on a flat floor and never a hole; the right cube floats above the floor with no shadow on the floor beneath it; the TV keeps its soft shadow halo on the wall. Remove the two small grey text tags above the cubes. Wall and floor fill the whole frame edge to edge and take the tone of the background field given below, the wall a touch lighter than the floor; the shadows stay darker than the surface they fall on in every variant. Frame the two cubes and the TV together, filling about 70 percent of the frame width. Demonstrates a procedural contact shadow that grounds objects
